clips.text: Being invited into someone's home is a real gesture, not a formality, and three small moves make you a good guest: something small in your hands, arriving on time, and letting your host lead the first toast.
¿Te gustaría cenar en mi casa el sábado?
Accept the invitation warmly. Speak now.
Claro que sí, con mucho gusto.
Don't arrive empty-handed. Something small — flowers, wine, a dessert — is the norm. Skip yellow flowers, which read as mourning here, not celebration.
At the door, hand over the small gift you brought. Speak now.
Le traje esto para la casa.
No te hubieras molestado, muchas gracias.
Everything else about time here can be relaxed. This isn't. Arriving on time for a home invitation reads as respect for the work someone put into tonight.
Pasa, siéntete como en tu casa.
Thank them for having you. Speak now.
Gracias por invitarme.
Glasses fill, and the table waits. The host leads the first toast — you don't need to invent one. When it comes, one word is the whole reply.
¡Salud!
The host raises a glass. Answer the toast. Speak now.
¡Salud!
Claro que sí, con mucho gusto. Le traje esto para la casa. Gracias por invitarme.

I08 complete. Bring something small. Arrive on time — this is the one place the relaxed clock doesn't apply. Let the host lead the toast, and salud covers your whole reply. Being a good guest here is three small, specific moves, not a performance.
A traveller is invited to dinner at a friend's home. Listen for the gift, the timing, and the toast.
¿Te gustaría cenar en mi casa el sábado?
Claro que sí, con mucho gusto.
Le traje esto para la casa.
¡Salud!
